'''Robert Clark Hughes''' (November 27, 1940 – August 27, 2026) was an American chemist.

== Early life and career ==
Hughes was born in [[Cleveland, Ohio]] on November 27, 1940,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/person/dr.-robert-clark-hughes-62250430|title=In Memory Of Dr. Robert Clark Hughes|work=Legacy|access-date=September 4, 2026|via=[[Legacy.com]]}}</ref> the son of Mike Everett Hughes. He attended [[Carleton College]], earning his degree in [[chemistry]]. He also attended [[Stanford University]], earning his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]]. After earning his degrees, he worked as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]] at [[Sandia National Laboratories]] in [[Albuquerque, New Mexico]].<ref name="a">{{Cite web|url=https://www.frenchfunerals.com/obituaries/dr-robert-hughes?ttm_pid=212170346&ttm_affiliate=legacypro&ttm_affiliatetype=standard&ttm_campaign=legacy|title=Dr. Robert Clark Hughes|work=French Funerals & Cremations|access-date=September 4, 2026}}</ref>

He worked at Sandia with numerous [[research group]]s,<ref name="a" /> and in 1982, he was named a [[Lists of fellows of the American Physical Society|fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=robert%20hughes&af=true|title=APS Fellow Archive|work=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=September 4, 2026}}</ref> He contributed to [[field-effect transistor]]s, [[Sensor#Chemical sensor|chemical sensor]]s, [[List of temperature sensors|temperature sensors]] and gas levels.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37269205800|title=R. C. Hughes|work=[[IEEE Xplore]]|access-date=September 4, 2026}}</ref> In 1997, he served as senior scientist at Sandia until his retirement in 2003.<ref name="a" />

== Personal life and death ==
Hughes was married to Laura. Their marriage lasted until Hughes's death in 2026.<ref name="a" />

Hughes died in [[Albuquerque, New Mexico]] on August 27, 2026, at the age of 85.<ref name="a" />
